name: Kanbei Kokubu
current_role: Representative Director, Chairman and CEO, KOKUBU Group Corp. (Tokyo food & beverage wholesaler)
profile: Kanbei Kokubu XII heads KOKUBU Group, one of Japan's largest food and alcoholic-beverage wholesalers, a family business founded in 1712 and passed down over three centuries. He was president from 1991 to 2017, then handed the presidency to Akira Kokubu and stayed on as chairman and CEO with representative authority.
interesting_fact: KOKUBU traces its roots to 1712, and its original 'Chomoku' company precepts date to 1774. Its current code of conduct, the 'Heisei no Chomoku', is an updated version of them.
deep_cut_fact: 'Kanbei' is a hereditary name passed to each head of the family; he is the 12th to hold it. He served as president for 26 years (1991 to 2017) before the 2017 handover to Akira Kokubu.
notes: Low public profile; Japanese-language outreach through the corporate inquiry form is the best route.

name: Anju Agarwal
current_role: Shareholder and promoter-group member, Macleods Pharmaceuticals (Mumbai); no public executive role found
profile: Anju Agarwal is the widow of Dr. Rajendra Agarwal, who co-founded Macleods Pharmaceuticals in 1986 with his brothers Girdharilal and Banwarilal Bawri to make anti-TB medicines. Macleods is privately held and among India's leading generics makers. She is listed in the promoter group of its 2022 draft IPO prospectus, and her husband died in November 2025.
interesting_fact: Macleods is named after John Macleod, a Scottish doctor and author of medical textbooks. The company grew into one of the world's major suppliers of affordable TB drugs.
notes: Very private; I found no public biography or interviews. She is a recently widowed shareholder, not an operating executive, and the bereavement is recent, so she is a poor podcast fit. The only route is through the Macleods corporate office.

name: Mary Alice (Dorrance) Malone
profile: Died June 16, 2025, aged 75. She was a Campbell Soup heiress, Campbell's longest-serving director (35 years) and the founder of Iron Spring Farm, an equestrian breeding centre.
notes: Deceased (June 2025) per Campbell's press release and the Philadelphia Inquirer obituary (https://www.inquirer.com/obituaries/mary-alice-dorrance-malone-death-campbells-equestrian-20250624.html). Skipped.

name: Sandro Veronesi
current_role: Founder and President, Oniverse (formerly Calzedonia Group), Verona
profile: Veronesi founded Calzedonia in the mid-1980s as a side business while still working at Golden Lady, Nerino Grassi's hosiery company. He built it into Oniverse, a group with Calzedonia, Intimissimi, Tezenis and Falconeri, more than 5,600 stores in 57 countries, and 2025 revenue of about EUR 3.7bn. The group has since added wine (Signorvino, wineries) and yachts (Pardo, Grand Soleil, VanDutch).
interesting_fact: He started Calzedonia as a side business while still employed at Golden Lady, then the world's leading tights maker. He later expanded into wine with Signorvino and into yacht building.
deep_cut_fact: When Calzedonia Group renamed itself in December 2023, the new name 'Oniverse' was chosen partly because it is an anagram of the Veronesi surname.
notes: hello@oniverse.it is the group's general contact address, not his personal one. The family also runs Fondazione San Zeno. Not to be confused with the Italian novelist of the same name.

name: Katherina Andresen
current_role: Board member and co-owner, Ferd (Andresen family investment company, Oslo)
profile: Katharina G. Andresen (born 1995, Oslo) is a sixth-generation member of Norway's Andresen family. In 2007 her father, Johan H. Andresen, transferred most of the family holding company Ferd to her and her sister Alexandra. Ferd invests in listed and private companies, real estate, impact investing and social entrepreneurs. She has sat on Ferd's board since 2023.
interesting_fact: In 2020 Forbes ranked her as the world's third-youngest billionaire. She and her sister own Ferd together with their father, as its fifth and sixth generations of family ownership.
deep_cut_fact: She has served as an advisor to Oslo Pride and is known as a supporter of LGBTQ+ rights. She has also competed as a dressage rider.
notes: Listed country 'Netherlands' is likely a data artefact; she is Norwegian (Oslo) and has reportedly also lived in London. Correct spelling is Katharina. She gives few interviews; the best route is Ferd's press office. Ferd's impact-investing and social-entrepreneur arms may be a natural podcast angle.

name: Park Soon-jae
current_role: Founder, Chairman of the Board and largest shareholder, Alteogen (Daejeon, South Korea); stepped down as CEO in December 2025
profile: Park (born 1954) founded Alteogen in Daejeon in 2008, after research at MIT and senior roles at LG Life Sciences and Hanwha's Dream Pharma. Alteogen's ALT-B4 'Hybrozyme' enzyme lets IV biologics be given as under-the-skin injections, and it is licensed to Merck for Keytruda (Keytruda SC). He was CEO from 2011 to December 2025 and now chairs the board, focusing on long-term strategy and next-generation pipeline.
interesting_fact: Alteogen's ALT-B4 enzyme is licensed by Merck for a subcutaneous version of the cancer drug Keytruda. When the deal was announced in 2024, Alteogen's shares jumped 25% in a day.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD from Purdue and says he left big-company life to escape slow decision-making and develop drugs 'with my own hands'. To avoid relying only on VC money, he funded early Alteogen by making biosimilars and pioneered licence-plus-profit-share deals with Brazil's Cristalia (2011) and Kyowa Kirin (2012).
notes: jsjang@alteogen.com is the IR & Corporate Communications director (Junseok Jang), listed as the media contact in Alteogen's 2026 press releases. Jeon Tae-yeon has been CEO since December 2025. Interviews with Park are mostly in Korean.

name: Xiuli Hawken
current_role: Former chair of Harbin Renhe Public Facilities Co.; former director and minority shareholder of Reading FC (per corporate listings)
profile: Xiuli Hawken, also known as Dai Xiuli (戴秀丽), is a Chinese businesswoman. She is reported to be the sister and business partner of Dai Yongge, who founded the Renhe group, which developed underground shopping centres in northern China and controlled the HK-listed Renhe Commercial Holdings. She appeared on Hurun lists from 2009 to 2014 and became a minority owner of English club Reading FC in 2021.
interesting_fact: Renhe's business was built on shopping centres converted from air-raid shelters, which it operates in some 30 Chinese cities including Harbin, the Dai family's hometown.
notes: Mostly inactive publicly since the mid-2010s, with no public contact channel. The family's Reading FC ownership ended in 2025 amid EFL sanctions and financial controversy, so this is a sensitive area to avoid. Not a good podcast candidate. I could not independently confirm the Hawken/Dai Xiuli identity link beyond Wikipedia's Chinese-name rendering.

name: Isabel dos Santos
current_role: Private investor (former chair of Sonangol, 2016-2017); reportedly based in Dubai
profile: Isabel dos Santos is the eldest daughter of Angola's late former president Jose Eduardo dos Santos. She built stakes in Angolan banking and telecoms (Unitel, BFA) and Portuguese companies such as NOS, and was once called Africa's richest woman. Since 2020 Angola and other states have pursued fraud and money-laundering cases and asset freezes against her, all of which she denies; Forbes dropped her from its billionaire list in 2021.
interesting_fact: Her father appointed her to head Sonangol, Angola's state oil company, in June 2016; the next president removed her in November 2017. She is nicknamed 'the princess' in Angola.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as an electrical engineer at King's College London before going into business.
notes: HIGH REPUTATIONAL RISK: she faces an Interpol notice, a UK worldwide asset freeze (appeal rejected 2024), a Dutch court finding over Sonangol funds and ongoing Angolan charges (some dropped in November 2025). She denies wrongdoing. Recommend not approaching her for an entrepreneurship podcast. Reported Instagram handles are inconsistent, so none are listed. No longer a billionaire per Forbes.

name: Lu Pingfang
current_role: Major shareholder (former co-actual controller), Shenzhen Minglida Precision Technology (SZ: 301268); no board or executive role found in 2026 filings
profile: Lu Pingfang (卢萍芳) is a major shareholder of Shenzhen-listed Minglida Precision, which she was previously listed alongside Tao Cheng as co-controlling. Minglida makes die-cast, injection-moulded and extruded precision structural parts, mainly for solar inverters, energy storage and EVs. It listed on the ChiNext board in April 2022, and she appeared on Hurun lists in 2022-2023.
interesting_fact: Minglida describes solar, energy storage and EVs as its core 'clean-energy' end markets. It has invested more than RMB 710m since 2023 in an aluminium-extrusion base in Mexico to serve North American EV and solar-storage customers.
notes: Very low public profile and not an executive; Tao Cheng is chairman and GM. Her shareholding comes from a personal matter reported in the press, which should be avoided. The company's energy-storage and solar hardware angle fits the podcast, but the company-facing person is Tao Cheng. The only route is the IR mailbox.

name: Eric Hémar
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, ID Logistics (Euronext Paris: IDL)
profile: Hémar started his career in the French civil service, at the Cour des comptes (supreme audit court) and then the transport ministry. He founded contract-logistics group ID Logistics in 2001 and floated it in Paris in 2012. The group made EUR 3.7bn of revenue in 2025 across 450 sites in 20 countries with 55,000 staff. He owns over 50% and has also chaired the TLF union of French transport and logistics firms since 2019.
interesting_fact: In November 2026 ID Logistics announced a partnership with Terra Robotics to pilot humanoid robots (Unitree G1 units nicknamed 'IDA' and 'Heinz') on sorting tasks at its German sites.
deep_cut_fact: Although ID Logistics is an SBF 120 company operating on five continents, its head office is in Orgon, a small village in the Provence countryside (Bouches-du-Rhône), rather than in Paris.
notes: A good podcast fit (warehouse automation, robotics, logistics energy use). The press agency Rumeur Publique is the best route. Web-search quota ran out partway through this lane, so the profile relies on Forbes and company documents.

name: Martin Hilti
profile: Died 19 August 1997 in Schaan, Liechtenstein, aged 82. He co-founded the Hilti construction-tools group (listed on Forbes 1996).
notes: Deceased in 1997 per German Wikipedia (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Hilti). Skipped. The Hilti group is now controlled by the Martin Hilti Family Trust.

name: Stephen Winn
current_role: Founder and former CEO of RealPage (stepped down after the 2021 sale to Thoma Bravo); private investor, Dallas
profile: Winn, an electrical engineer (BA UT Austin, MS Stanford), began at his father's accounting software firm, Computer Language Research, and became its CEO. He founded RealPage in 1998 to sell property-management software to landlords, took it public in 2010 and sold it to Thoma Bravo in April 2021 (reported at about $10.2bn). He stepped down as CEO shortly afterwards and is now about 80 and based in Dallas.
interesting_fact: RealPage grew out of 'Little Buddy', a side venture inside a tax-software business Winn had acquired to expand Computer Language Research.
notes: Retired from operating roles with a low public profile, and I found no personal or family-office contact channel. RealPage is the subject of DOJ and state antitrust litigation over rent-pricing software, a sensitive topic. Web-search quota ran out before deeper research on this person.

name: Huang Zelan
current_role: Chairman and ultimate controlling shareholder, Chongyi Zhangyuan Tungsten Co. (SZSE: 002378), Ganzhou, Jiangxi
profile: Huang Zelan (黄泽兰) is the founding shareholder and chairman of Zhangyuan Tungsten, based in Chongyi county, Jiangxi, China's tungsten heartland. The company runs the whole tungsten chain, from its own mines and concentrate through APT, tungsten and carbide powders to cemented-carbide tools. He controls it through Chongyi Zhangyuan Investment Holding, of which he owns 94%.
interesting_fact: Zhangyuan has moved into high-strength tungsten wire built for diamond-wire cutting of solar silicon wafers, a fast-growing replacement for steel wire in PV manufacturing, and is building a smart-manufacturing project for it.
deep_cut_fact: Zhangyuan was originally set up by Huang Zelan with a small group of individual co-founders and is still headquartered in Chongyi county town rather than a big city. The group also includes a local power company, Chongyi Niubilong Electric Power.
notes: Very low public profile and Chinese-language only. Tungsten is a critical mineral, and the PV tungsten-wire business gives an energy angle. Day-to-day operations are run by the vice-chairman and GM, a younger family member. The deep-cut fact is company-level rather than personal.

name: Lu Keping
current_role: Founder/patriarch of Jiangsu Sunshine Group (wool textiles), Jiangyin; current formal title not confirmed
profile: Lu Keping (陆克平, born November 1944, Jiangyin, Jiangsu) became director of the Jiangyin Wool Mill in 1986 and built it into Sunshine Group (阳光集团), one of China's largest worsted-wool fabric and apparel makers. Its listed arm is Jiangsu Sunshine (SSE: 600220). He appeared on Hurun lists from 2005 to 2023 together with Yu Qinfen.
interesting_fact: He took over the small Jiangyin Wool Mill as factory director and party branch secretary in 1986 and grew it into Sunshine Group, often described in Chinese media as a 'wool-textile giant'.
notes: Now in his 80s and only covered in Chinese. In 2019 the CSRC fined him RMB 27.34m and imposed a lifetime securities-market ban over undisclosed control of Sihuan Bio (per Wikipedia), and the listed company is now flagged 'ST'. A reputational concern and a poor podcast fit. I could not find or verify an official group website or contact.

name: Jordi Rubiralta
current_role: Board member (former President 2012-2019), Werfen; head of family office Yukon Capital
profile: Jordi Rubiralta's fortune comes from Werfen, the Barcelona-based in-vitro diagnostics group (hemostasis, acute care, autoimmunity, transfusion) that his father José María Rubiralta founded as Izasa in 1966. He became president in 2012 and led acquisitions of TEM (Germany, 2016) and Accriva Diagnostics (US, 2017), before handing the presidency to Marc Rubiralta in 2019. He remains on the board, and his family office Yukon Capital is active in Spanish real estate.
interesting_fact: Werfen began in 1966 as Izasa, a small Barcelona distributor of clinical diagnostic products. It moved into manufacturing in 1973 with Biokit and became a global player in 1991 by buying Boston-based Instrumentation Laboratory.
deep_cut_fact: Werfen's own timeline marks his 2012 appointment as president as its official 'Generational Change' milestone. During his presidency the company built a new Iberian logistics centre in Cuenca (2016) and new Biokit facilities near Barcelona (2017).
notes: Werfen is headquartered in L'Hospitalet de Llobregat (Barcelona), not Madrid as Forbes states. He keeps a low profile. No press email is published, so the contact form is the route; Yukon Capital might also be reachable. Web-search quota ran out, so this relies on Forbes and the Werfen site.

name: Lim Kaling
current_role: Non-executive director and major shareholder, Razer; head of the Lim Teck Lee family group (Singapore)
profile: Lim Kaling (62, Singapore; BBA, UC Berkeley) was an early backer of gaming-hardware brand Razer, co-founded by Min-Liang Tan in 2005, and is its non-executive director. Razer listed in Hong Kong in 2017, raising $529m, and Lim and Tan took it private in 2022 at a $3.2bn valuation. He also runs the Lim Teck Lee group, a family business in real estate, manufacturing and trading.
interesting_fact: He and Razer co-founder Min-Liang Tan took Razer private in 2022, five years after its $529m Hong Kong IPO, in a deal valuing it at $3.2bn.
notes: Very private and rarely interviewed; Min-Liang Tan is Razer's public face. Razer's press office is the only published route and will only answer press. Web-search quota ran out before I could find a sourced personal deep-cut fact.

name: Lilian Werninghaus
current_role: Heir/shareholder in the WEG founding-family holdings (presumed); no public role found
profile: Lilian Werninghaus appeared once on the Forbes billionaires list (2014) under 'industrial machinery', Brazil. This almost certainly reflects a stake in WEG, the Jaraguá do Sul electric-motor and power-equipment maker co-founded in 1961 by Geraldo Werninghaus with Werner Ricardo Voigt and Eggon João da Silva. Geraldo died in 1999, and her exact relationship to him and current holdings could not be verified.
interesting_fact: WEG's name combines the first letters of its three founders' names: Werner, Eggon and Geraldo. Geraldo Werninghaus later served as a Santa Catarina state deputy (1995-1999).
notes: Identity is only partly confirmed: the WEG link is inferred from the surname and Forbes category. Very private, and on the list only in 2014. WEG (motors, transformers, solar and storage, grid equipment) is highly relevant to energy and data centres, but the family's public faces are other WEG founder-family members. The WEG name etymology is from my general knowledge; the source confirms only the three founders.

name: Ranga Raju Kanumuri
current_role: Chairman, Sai Life Sciences (Hyderabad; NSE/BSE-listed CRDMO)
profile: Dr. K. Ranga Raju, a pharmaceutical scientist turned entrepreneur, founded Sai Life Sciences in Hyderabad in 1999 as a medicinal-chemistry partner to US biotechs. It is now an integrated contract research, development and manufacturing organisation (CRDMO) with sites in India, the UK and the US. Sai Life listed in India in December 2024, raising about INR 30.4bn; his son Krishna Kanumuri is MD and CEO.
interesting_fact: He holds a Doctor of Pharmacy plus bachelor's and master's degrees from the Massachusetts College of Pharmacy in Boston, after a first pharmacy degree from the University of Mysore.
deep_cut_fact: Sai Life Sciences was originally founded in 1999 as 'Sai Dru Syn Laboratories'. It began as a small medicinal-chemistry services provider for US biotechs and was renamed later to reflect a broader life-sciences focus.
notes: Low personal profile; CEO Krishna Kanumuri is the company's public voice and may be the easier guest. Route requests via IR or general inquiries.
